items.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024
items.q: I bring it up because I’ve lost track of how many people have said, “Don’t go into jazz unless you don’t have any other choice.” Even Phil Woods. He said, “If you’re debating about being a brain surgeon or a tenor man, go with the brain surgery.”

ctx.x: Sure. Yes. Absolutely. And Michigan being a Research 1 institution and obviously an excellent institution for many different types of things, is a place that students often will come and double major, sometimes because they really have a passionate interest in both jazz and something else, and partly because maybe their parents want them to have the — well it’s hard to know which is the back-up degree sometimes, but they want them to have that other degree so that they will be ensured of getting a job when they…

If you had a nephew or a niece that was oh let’s say 15 and their aspirations were to become a musician, do you have any advice at that point in their lives? I bring it up because I’ve lost track of how many people have said, “Don’t go into jazz unless you don’t have any other choice.” Even Phil Woods. He said, “If you’re debating about being a brain surgeon or a tenor man, go with the brain surgery.”

Yeah, I mean definitely. You’ve got to be passionate about it. You know this is not the complete flip side but I’ve also been around John Clayton when he has talked about students saying that they’re going to go into — you know they’re going to do jazz but they’re going to do music education as a fallback. And he’s saying okay, you’re a parent, do you want your child being taught by somebody for whom education, you know teaching is just a fallback? Something they didn’t really want to do. And so you know he’s…
